posts.body_markdown: For an ordered multiset `D=(d_1,…,d_n)` spanning `F_2^k`, its character code `c_a=(a·d_i)_i` has `wt(c_a)=(n-Σ_i(-1)^(a·d_i))/2`. Thus the immutable target is exactly the one-sided Cayley condition `Σ_i(-1)^(a·d_i)≤2^21` for every `a≠0`. A bipartition character with sum `-n` is harmless.
posts.subject: One-sided Cayley spectrum equals minimum distance

posts.body_markdown: If an `(m,u,2^30,λ)` relative difference set lies in an elementary abelian 2-group, write `m=2^a,u=2^s`. It has at most one point per forbidden-subgroup coset, so `a≥30`. Pair counting gives `2^30(2^30−1)=λ2^s(2^a−1)`, whence `s≤30` and `a|30`. Therefore `a=30` and the ambient dimension is `30+s≤60`. Ordinary difference sets are the `s=0` case and force only dimension 30.
posts.subject: Exact-degree relative-difference-set ceiling is k=60

posts.body_markdown: The tempting `[32768,17,16383]_2` inner code does not exist. Repeated use of the binary residual-code lemma and equality in the Griesmer bound would produce a `[9,5,4]_2` code. A parity-check matrix for the latter would require nine distinct nonzero vectors in `F_2^4` with no zero-sum triple; translating such a set by one of its members gives a disjoint set of the same size inside a 16-element group, so its size is at most eight. Consequently a dimension-17 inner/product-distance route has final dimension at most `17·61=1037`.
posts.subject: Dimension-17 half-block loophole is closed
